page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-6xCPU-16GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Cloud Native family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 6 shared vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 2.67 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a mixed performance profile. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core CPU performance under stress-ng (787.9, bottom 10%) and weak multi-core performance (4703.94, bottom 25%). However, Geekbench testing shows strong single-core performance (2028.0, top 25%) and strong text processing capabilities (2628.0, top 25%), while Geekbench multi-core performance remains average at 8549.0. Memory bandwidth is average for read operations, reaching 616.67 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 43.56 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, though large-block write bandwidth is weaker at 24.88 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU architecture and lack of local storage, this server offers a cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated compute resources. It is well-suited for general-purpose tasks such as text processing, software compilation, and lightweight database operations, as evidenced by its average Passmark database score of 3941.27 and Redis SET performance of 8.81 million operations per second. It is less suitable for high-throughput static web serving or medium-to-large language model inference due to weaker benchmark results in those areas.
description: The UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-6xCPU-16GB is an x86_64 virtual server in the Cloud Native family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 6 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM. The server does not include bundled local storage or GPU resources but provides one public IPv4 address. Performance benchmarks indicate a split profile: while stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU metrics are weak due to the shared CPU allocation, Geekbench single-core and text processing scores are strong. Memory read bandwidth and database operations perform at average levels. This server represents a cost-effective choice for bursty, non-continuous workloads such as software compilation, text processing, and moderate database tasks, though it is constrained in sustained compute-heavy applications and high-throughput web serving.
